riot.name: Riot Client

alternatives.name: League of Legends bootstrapper (NA)
alternatives.notes: Riot's own download-page link (winget RiotGames.LeagueOfLegends.NA, all Lutris scripts); installs the same shared Riot Client but then downloads League of Legends, which cannot run under Wine (Vanguard). Region variants: live.{na,euw,eune,br,la1,la2,oc1,ru,tr,jp,kr,tw2,ph2,sg2,vn2}.exe.

installer.notes: Default: the Legends of Runeterra bootstrapper (Americas; europe / asia variants: live.live.europe.exe, live.live.asia.exe), because League cannot run under Wine at all (Vanguard) and LoR is the one Riot title without the kernel driver; it installs the same shared Riot Client. The League bootstrapper is kept under installer.alternatives. Riot publishes no standalone Riot Client installer (riot-client.secure.dyn.riotcdn.net/channels/public/x/installer/current/live*.exe returns 404). Every Riot game bootstrapper (~75 MB, PE32+ x86-64) installs the shared Riot Client into C:\Riot Games\Riot Client\ and then has the client download that product. This URL is the one on Riot's own download page, in all 15 Lutris scripts and in the winget manifest RiotGames.LeagueOfLegends.NA. It is a rolling 'current' link that Riot republishes in place (Content-Disposition 'Install League of Legends na.exe', Last-Modified 2026-08-12), so a hard-pinned hash would break on Riot's next bootstrapper update; as of 2026-10-10 the served file (75,831,040 bytes) hashes to sha256 cc897ef385ff3ae1481106c251a86ac7382f2b736053e9e577aada327cabeb54, identical to winget 138.0.0.4786 (use as a point-in-time check only). Region variants (Lutris): live.{na,euw,eune,br,la1,la2,oc1,ru,tr,jp,kr,tw2,ph2,sg2,vn2}.exe. Bootstrappers of other Riot titles install the same client: VALORANT https://valorant.secure.dyn.riotcdn.net/channels/public/x/installer/current/live.live.{na,eu,ap,kr,br,latam}.exe ('Install VALORANT.exe', winget RiotGames.Valorant.NA, same switches); Legends of Runeterra https://bacon.secure.dyn.riotcdn.net/channels/public/x/installer/current/live.live.{americas,europe,asia}.exe ('Legends_Of_Runeterra_Installer.exe', used by the Lutris 'Riot Games' installer and the LoR snap). Because League cannot run under Wine at all (Vanguard), the LoR bootstrapper is the only sensible default for a Linux install: it pulls the one Riot Client title that has no kernel anti-cheat instead of tens of GB of League. Silent switches (winget manifest): Silent/SilentWithProgress '--skip-to-install', InstallLocation '--install-path="<dir>"', Log '--log-root="<dir>"', Custom '--disable-auto-launch'; silentinstallhq.com additionally lists '--disable-self-update' and '--disable-patching' (not independently verified). Scope is per-user, so uninstall entries land under HKCU. Lutris runs the bootstrapper interactively with the instruction 'Do not log in during installation, just close the installation client once it finishes downloading', then kills Wine. Whether '--skip-to-install' also downloads the game or only the client was not verified.

installed_games.notes: Primary source: drive_c/ProgramData/Riot Games/RiotClientInstalls.json, e.g. {"associated_client": {"D:/Riot Games/VALORANT": "C:/Riot Games/Riot Client/RiotClientServices.exe", "C:/Riot Games/Riot Client": "C:/Riot Games/Riot Client/RiotClientServices.exe"}, "rc_default": "C:/Riot Games/Riot Client/RiotClientServices.exe"} (optional "rc_live" too; paths use Windows drive letters with forward slashes). Every associated_client key whose basename is not 'Riot Client' is a game install dir; rc_live/rc_default give the client exe. Per-product details: drive_c/ProgramData/Riot Games/Metadata/<product>.<patchline>/<product>.<patchline>.product_settings.yaml with product_install_full_path (e.g. "D:/Riot Games/VALORANT/live"), product_install_root, shortcut_enabled; after an uninstall the folder can remain holding only product_install_root (treat as not installed); an update-status.json may sit beside it. The folder name is the game id + patchline: league_of_legends.live (also serves Teamfight Tactics), valorant.live, bacon.live (Legends of Runeterra), lion.live (2XKO). Launch ids for game_args are exactly these product names (league_of_legends, valorant, bacon, lion). Game exe inside the install dir: LeagueClient.exe, VALORANT.exe, LoR.exe, Lion.exe. Display names: League of Legends, VALORANT, Legends of Runeterra, 2XKO. Registry alternative (per-user installer): HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\Riot Game <product>.<patchline> -> InstallLocation; UninstallString is '"C:\Riot Games\Riot Client\RiotClientServices.exe" --uninstall-product=<product> --uninstall-patchline=<patchline>'. The client itself registers a riotclient:// protocol: HKCR\riotclient\shell\open\command (or HKLM\SOFTWARE\Classes\riotclient\shell\open\command) default value quotes the RiotClientServices.exe path; the URL grammar of that scheme was not verified, hence game_url null.

signin.summary: Riot games are free-to-play, so Game Pass unlocks in-game perks rather than games; the link is made on account.riotgames.com. On Linux only Legends of Runeterra can run - League of Legends, Teamfight Tactics, VALORANT and 2XKO need the Vanguard kernel driver.
steps: Click Open Riot Client and sign in with your Riot Account (create one at https://signup.riotgames.com if needed). Let any download in the client finish before signing in.

In your web browser open https://account.riotgames.com/xbox-game-pass, click 'Go to the Xbox Social Sign-in Page', sign in with the Microsoft account that holds the Game Pass subscription, allow Riot Games to access the Xbox profile and sign in with your Riot Account.
The perks (all champions and agents, XP boosts, ...) unlock at the next game login, up to 24 hours later. Nothing is added to a library: every Riot title is already free to install from the client.

On Linux install only Legends of Runeterra (what this recipe's bootstrapper fetches); League of Legends, Teamfight Tactics, VALORANT and 2XKO need the Vanguard kernel driver and cannot start under Wine.
signin.xbox_link: Account linking at https://account.riotgames.com/xbox-game-pass (Riot Account <-> Xbox profile). It is not a game license: Riot games are free-to-play and there is no Xbox-app install/launch path through the Riot Client; the link only unlocks in-game benefits for an active Game Pass membership (Xbox Wire, Dec 2022: all Game Pass members). Riot's FAQ (updated 2024-09-30) and the riotgames.com benefits page publish no end date.
notes: Run RiotClientServices.exe with no arguments in the launcher prefix (a bare launch opens the Riot Client home/library; a --launch-product launch goes straight to that game's patch-and-login flow). The CEF-based sign-in window appears: sign in with the Riot Account (username + password, optional 'Stay signed in'); create one at https://signup.riotgames.com if needed. Do not sign in while a bootstrapper is still downloading (Lutris instruction).

Link the Xbox profile in a normal browser, not inside the prefix: open https://account.riotgames.com/xbox-game-pass -> 'Go to the Xbox Social Sign-in Page' -> log in with the Microsoft account that has an Xbox profile and the active Game Pass membership -> click Yes to allow Riot Games to access the Xbox Live information -> sign in with the Riot Account.

Benefits unlock on the next login to any Riot game (pop-up notification; can take up to 24 h). League shows a persistent Rewards Program icon in the client with 'Game Pass' listed while the link and membership are active.

Nothing 'appears' as a Game Pass entitlement: all Riot PC titles are free-to-play and the Riot Client shows every one of them to every account. Game Pass only adds in-game perks (all LoL champions, all VALORANT agents, TFT tacticians/arena skin, LoR Foundations cards, 20% XP boosts) that lapse when the membership lapses. Installing a title from its Riot Client tile starts its download; on Linux only Legends of Runeterra (bacon) is worth installing.

anticheat.notes: Riot Vanguard = a user-mode client plus a Windows kernel-mode driver (vgk.sys). Required by League of Legends (mandatory worldwide since patch 14.9, 1 May 2024; TPM 2.0 / Secure Boot on Windows 11), Teamfight Tactics PC (Riot FAQ: 'Vanguard works in tandem with the League Client, so it will need to be running for Teamfight Tactics PC as well'), VALORANT (since launch; its spec page lists Windows 10/11 only) and 2XKO (product 'lion'; AreWeAntiCheatYet: Denied). It is impossible under Wine/Proton: Wine cannot load Windows kernel drivers, and Riot's own dev post states 'the current Lutris-based implementation for League (that uses wine) will not be able to satisfy the Vanguard driver requirements', 'Linux does not currently afford us sufficient ability to attest boot state or kernel modules', and that VMs/emulation are rejected as well ('an exceptionally dangerous game'); Riot cited 'just over 800 Linux users'. AreWeAntiCheatYet lists League, TFT, VALORANT and 2XKO as Denied; lutris.net flags League as 'kernel-level anticheat, unsupported on Linux'. Vanguard is not EasyAntiCheat or BattlEye, so Steam's 'Proton EasyAntiCheat Runtime' / 'Proton BattlEye Runtime' do nothing here, and there is no single-player bypass: these are online-only games whose exes refuse to start without the driver. 'Vanguard On-Demand' (2026) only changes when the driver loads on qualifying Windows 11 25H2 machines; it does not help Linux. Legends of Runeterra (bacon) does not use Vanguard: leagueoflinux.org lists its desktop version as fully playable via the Lutris 'Riot Games' installer, but AreWeAntiCheatYet marks it 'Broken' with 'Packman' (Riot's legacy anti-tamper) since 2024-11-11 without a reference, and a Feb 2026 Lutris forum thread reports an immediate crash at launch, so its current status is unverified. Practical rule for the UI: mark League/TFT/VALORANT/2XKO as 'cannot run on Linux (Vanguard kernel anti-cheat)' and never attempt them; offer LoR as untested.

known_issues: League of Legends, Teamfight Tactics (PC), VALORANT and 2XKO cannot run under Wine/Proton at all because of the Vanguard kernel driver; no bypass, no Proton anti-cheat runtime applies, and online modes are the whole game.

Riot Client window renders black when the prefix has no Arial/Times fonts (Wine bug 54792, duplicate of 32342: CEF font validation); fix is winetricks corefonts. Lutris scripts do not install it; GE-Proton ships Liberation substitutes, so add 'corefonts' only if the client comes up black.

The bootstrapper auto-launches the Riot Client after installing unless --disable-auto-launch is passed; Lutris tells users to close the client once its download finishes and then kills all Wine processes before first launch.

The Riot Client keeps running as a tray icon/background RiotClientServices.exe after a game exits (Lutris LoR note: 'don't forget to quit Riot icon notification in taskbar'); stop_wine() the prefix after play.
Legends of Runeterra may crash on its first start; Lutris advises closing all Wine processes and starting again. Its 2025/2026 playability is contested (see anticheat).

GE-Proton behaviour is untested here: no Riot entry exists in umu-protonfixes gamefixes-umu or umu-database; Lutris 0.5.20+ runs these same scripts on GE-Proton via umu by default, which is the only indirect evidence that the CEF client works there. GE-Proton release assets are GE-ProtonX-Y-x86_64.tar.gz with a .sha512sum file (sha512, not sha256).

Historical only: pre-Vanguard League needed patched wine-ge 'LoL' builds (lutris-GE-Proton8-27-LoL, GE-LOL) and older Lutris scripts added d3dx9/d3dcompiler; StartWine/PortWINE/lux-wine DB entries still reference those builds. None of it applies to the launcher itself.

The Lutris registry/env tweaks in this recipe (GrabFullScreen, MouseWarpOverride, grey background, STAGING_SHARED_MEMORY, WINE_LARGE_ADDRESS_AWARE) target the in-game League window, not the client; they are harmless under Proton (LAA is already Proton's default) and can be dropped.

Installer region only selects which League shard the bootstrapper downloads; the account's region is fixed by the Riot Account, and the client UI language is chosen with --locale=xx_XX (Lutris offers cs_CZ, en_AU, en_GB, en_US, fr_FR, de_DE, es_ES, es_MX, it_IT, ja_JP, hu_HU, pl_PL, pt_BR, ro_RO, ru_RU, tr_TR).
Paths in RiotClientInstalls.json and product_settings.yaml use Windows drive letters with forward slashes; map C:/ to <prefix>/drive_c/ before using them.
